# STORY-AEX.8 — AEXOS Expanded Squad Library

**Epic:** [EPIC-AEXOS-EVOLUTION](./EPIC-AEXOS-EVOLUTION.md)
**Architecture:** [ADR-AEX-008](./adr/ADR-AEX-008-AEXOS-SQUAD-LIBRARY-IN-CORE.md) · [Source Tree](../../source-tree.md)
**Status:** Done
**Executor:** `@dev`
**Quality Gate:** `@architect`
**Quality Gate Tools:** `validate:squads`, `validate:squad-manifests`, `validate:squad-registry`, `validate:squad-agents`, Jest, ESLint, TypeScript, publish validator

## Story

As the AEXOS Product Owner, I want the expanded AEXOS squad library to ship as
an integral proprietary capability of AEXOS, owned by Cyryx Labs LLC, so that
every squad is installed, routed and projected automatically through the same
architecture as the existing Core squads.

## Scope

The release adds eleven complete squads:

1. `apex`
2. `brand`
3. `curator`
4. `deep-research`
5. `dispatch`
6. `education`
7. `kaizen`
8. `kaizen-v2`
9. `legal-analyst`
10. `seo`
11. `squad-creator`

Only complete task-first squads may be registered. Documentation-only or
marketing-only directories are not runtime capabilities.

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| AC1 | All eleven squads exist under `squads/` without removing or overwriting any pre-existing AEXOS squad. |
| AC2 | Every added squad uses canonical `squad.yaml`, contains `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and has non-empty `agents/`, `tasks/`, and `workflows/` directories. |
| AC3 | All operational content uses AEXOS, `.aexos-core`, `@aexos/core`, and Cyryx Labs LLC product identity, with no legacy product or company branding. |
| AC4 | Every manifest declares Cyryx Labs LLC as author and `UNLICENSED` at squad level, inheriting the proprietary root AEXOS license. |
| AC5 | No squad contains a separate `LICENSE` file or historical ownership, repository, contributor, acquisition, commit or licensing record. |
| AC6 | Every added agent exposes a parseable fenced YAML definition with `agent.id` matching its filename plus non-empty `agent.name` and `agent.title`. |
| AC7 | `kaizen` and `kaizen-v2` are separately addressable; every V2 agent and entry point is namespaced to eliminate global routing ambiguity. |
| AC8 | All eleven squads are present in `.aexos-core/data/squad-registry.yaml` and projected to supported IDE/Codex surfaces by the existing generators. |
| AC9 | No temp-machine path, import tooling or non-AEXOS product metadata remains in the versioned result. |
| AC10 | Focused squad gates, IDE/parity gates, lint, typecheck, full tests and build pass, or exact inherited failures are reported without being represented as success. |
| AC11 | Unrelated user work present before the story remains untouched. No commit, push, PR, publish or deployment is performed. |

## Dev Notes

### Architecture alignment

- Canonical squad source of truth is `squads/{name}/`; the npm package includes
  `squads/`, and the installer scaffolds manifests discovered there.
  [Source: `docs/framework/source-tree.md#Squads-System`; `package.json#files`]
- Manifests use task-first architecture and are normalized from disk by
  `scripts/normalize-squad-manifests.js`.
  [Source: `.aexos-core/schemas/squad-schema.json`; `scripts/normalize-squad-manifests.js`]
- Routing is derived from installed manifests and generated by
  `scripts/generate-squad-registry.js`; the registry is not hand-edited.
- Squad agents are projected from their canonical source through
  `scripts/sync-squad-agents.js`.

### Product and ownership decision

ADR-AEX-007 remains the proposal for future subscription-gated expansions.
ADR-AEX-008 classifies this named eleven-squad library as proprietary AEXOS Core
owned by Cyryx Labs LLC, by direct Product Owner instruction.

### Compatibility adaptations

- Agent YAML must parse under `js-yaml` and satisfy the AEXOS agent identity
  contract; invalid input is repaired without discarding operational content.
- Kaizen generations require distinct global identities.
- Legacy `config.yaml` manifests are converted to canonical `squad.yaml`.
- Every squad receives a clean AEXOS `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Incomplete directories are excluded from runtime discovery.

## Testing Requirements

```powershell
npm run validate:squads
npm run validate:squad-manifests
npm run validate:squad-registry
npm run validate:squad-agents
npm run validate:codex-skills
npm run sync:ide:check
npm run validate:parity
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

Additional tests assert the exact squad set, absence of legacy brand and
ownership records, absence of per-squad licenses, Kaizen V2 identity uniqueness
and registry completeness.

## Security and Safety

- Added scripts are repository content, not trusted executables. Deployment,
  remote, scraping or destructive scripts are not executed during validation.
- No secrets or source-machine absolute paths may be introduced.
- Rebranding is followed by syntax and parse checks.
- The user's unrelated untracked paths remain untouched.
